title: arXiv AI: Monday 12 October 2026 — 10 notable papers
global_caveat: This is an inferred relevance ranking, not an official arXiv trending chart; the latest batch is too new for strong citation evidence, so popularity cannot be measured.

sections.title: RATED: Reliability-Aware AI Agent Tool Retrieval via Execution Dynamics
sections.abstract: RATED combines semantic tool retrieval with a contextual bandit that re-ranks tools using execution feedback, and introduces a benchmark of 5,172 tools and more than 210,000 query-tool pairs.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report a 52.2% relative MRR improvement over ToolLLM’s API retriever and a reduction in fault selection from 86.2% to 2.9% in a 30%-failure scenario, with under 1 ms added latency.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported outage results are benchmark experiments; they do not establish reliability across every live tool ecosystem or failure distribution.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Accepted at CIKM 2026 with DOI; large tool benchmark and reported outage comparisons.

sections.title: X-AgentRed: Red-Teaming Personal Agents in Evolving Multi-Service Ecosystems
sections.abstract: X-AgentRed uses a dependency graph and execution feedback to generate and refine harmful multi-tool workflows for testing personal agents.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report 1.77× the harmful-path rate and 2.99× tool coverage versus compared baselines across four frontier agents.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors note graph-maintenance costs as services change; evaluation uses a fixed simulated ecosystem.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Comparative evaluation of four agents across 30 services and 914 tools with reported baseline improvements.

sections.title: RSI-Anything: Unlocking Recursive Self-Improvement with World Models
sections.abstract: RSI-Anything uses predictive world models to select actions and learning data, improve policies or workflows from feedback, and retain compatible updates across iterations.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report code-repair success rising from 26.3% with a static verifier to 31.2% after predictive selection and world-model adaptation, and laboratory-planning scores increasing across five policy versions.
sections.unique_caveat: Results are specific to the paper’s selected tasks and evaluation setups; they do not establish general recursive self-improvement across arbitrary environments.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Reported experiments span code repair, GUI tasks, laboratory planning, reaction optimization, and an immune-science workflow; code is linked from the abstract.

sections.title: Splat2Act: From Captured Scenes to Personalized VLA Manipulation
sections.abstract: Splat2Act builds simulation-ready scene replicas from phone scans and uses generated demonstrations to personalize a vision-language-action policy to a user’s environment and objects.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors present an automated real-to-sim-to-real pipeline; their study covers 101 scanned environments and reports 63.9% success on a 12-task real Stretch 3 subset.
sections.unique_caveat: Real-robot evaluation is limited to a 12-task subset on one platform; the 62.5% aggregate target-scene result is not a universal deployment rate.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: 101 scanned environments, more than 68,000 generated pickup demonstrations, and real-robot evaluation.

sections.title: BT-Agent: Deploying Onboard Robot Agents with Behavior Trees and Multi-Fidelity Evaluation
sections.abstract: BT-Agent combines LLM task decisions with behavior-tree skills, structured failure feedback, and a multi-fidelity benchmark comparing text tasks with simulated robot execution.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report success gains over the strongest Act/ReAct baseline of about 10 percentage points at 4B and 5 points at 9B, and 10.9× higher evaluation throughput in text mode.
sections.unique_caveat: Text evaluation is not equivalent to physical execution; Habitat covers 39 tasks, and onboard operation is demonstrated on a quadruped.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Onboard 9B operation, 161-task benchmark, Habitat simulations, and reported ablations.

sections.title: Adaptive DHiSparse: Speculative Decoding over a Load-Adaptive KV Hierarchy
sections.abstract: Adaptive DHiSparse combines speculative decoding with a hierarchical KV cache whose GPU residency changes with serving load, aiming to sustain long-context throughput under memory pressure.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report up to 4× concurrency versus HiSparse at matched latency bounds and 1.85× output versus resident serving in a stated 500K-context configuration.
sections.unique_caveat: Speedups are tied to specific models, context lengths, concurrency levels, and latency bounds; broader hardware and workload behavior remains to be established.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed in four core AI categories and reports workload-specific throughput/concurrency comparisons at 100K- and 500K-token contexts.

sections.title: A Privileged Teacher That Only Scores Cannot Search: Critique-Conditioned On-Policy Self-Distillation for Reasoning
sections.abstract: The paper argues that score-only privileged teachers fail to localize and correct reasoning errors, then conditions the teacher on generated critiques to create a more corrective distillation signal.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that critique-conditioned scoring localizes errors and shifts probability toward tokens associated with backtracking, unlike the tested score-only signals.
sections.unique_caveat: Workshop acceptance and reported experiments are preliminary evidence; the abstract does not establish robust gains across models, domains, or training regimes.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed across three core AI categories; reports error-localization, test-time recovery, and cold-start GRPO experiments; arXiv comment notes NeurIPS 2026 FLLMPT workshop oral acceptance.

sections.title: LapMerge: Differentiable Exact-Budget Token Merging in Linear Time
sections.abstract: LapMerge groups ordered tokens into an exact output budget using a learned mass distribution and linear-time scans, retaining differentiability while reducing sequence length.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose a differentiable reducer with forward and backward complexity O(M+N), and report speedups up to two orders of magnitude at large sequence lengths.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors say it is most effective when token order reflects spatial or temporal locality; results may not transfer to inputs without that structure.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Reports comparisons with token reducers on vision and vision-language tasks and large-sequence speed measurements.

sections.title: Can Language Models Play the Wikipedia Game?
sections.abstract: The authors use link-navigation games across five Wikipedia languages and academic-paper citation graphs to compare model retrieval/navigation with human and TF-IDF baselines.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that the best tested models achieved human-comparable success but did not significantly outperform humans, with rankings varying across languages and topics.
sections.unique_caveat: Link navigation is an analogue of information retrieval, not a complete test of open-domain retrieval; model rankings vary by language and topic.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Five languages, five academic-literature datasets, local graph code, and human and TF-IDF comparisons.

sections.title: Can Language Models Learn When to Abstain? Policy Learning and Calibrated Answer Selection
sections.abstract: On factual question answering, the study compares training the model and a separate answer selector to improve the decision to answer or abstain.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report improved threshold-averaged utility over a calibrated confidence filter on TriviaQA and NQ-Open; on TriviaQA coverage rises from 20.2% to 30.9% while scored-answer error falls from 23.0% to 14.5% under exact match.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors report inconsistent reinforcement-learning gains and that on NQ-Open the selector remains worse than always abstaining.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Three training seeds, two held-out confidence thresholds, a partial human-reviewed audit, and evaluation on TriviaQA and NQ-Open.
